criteria.evidence: The response doesn't have access to actual code/logs, but it asks the user to identify the symptom ('What's the actual symptom?') and requests specifics at the end, rather than reproducing the failure itself.
Step 2 explicitly says 'Check the recent change itself - Diff exactly what changed (tool schema/definitions, system prompt, SDK/library version...)' with detailed breakdown of common causes.
Provides the pipeline diagram 'LLM emits tool call → your app parses it → app dispatches to tool/API → result returned → app feeds result back to LLM' and instructs to isolate which boundary breaks.

Step 4 'Compare against known-good' implies forming a hypothesis (model-side vs app-side) before testing, and step 1 ties symptoms to hypotheses, but there's no explicit statement of a single testable hypothesis before proposing fixes—fixes are only listed generically in step 5 after diagnosis.
criteria.criterion: Form a testable hypothesis before fixing.
